cases.note: Exact current finality evidence is bound to the decision and authority.
A decision may exist without any separate finality evidence.
Finality can be issued for a different decision.
Finality can carry a different semantic decision identity.
Finality state may be presented as mutable.
Finality may be given a wider horizon than the decision.
Finality may be issued by an untrusted principal.
Authority may be addressed through a mutable latest reference.
Finality may be timestamped before decision evaluation.
A bounded finality assertion can expire.
A revocation is represented as a distinct transition.
A supersession is represented as a distinct transition.
A successor's finality can be presented against the predecessor.
Applicable finality states can conflict.
Equivalent applicable assertions can arrive in a different order.
An identical finality assertion can be replayed.
The same finality identifier can be reused with changed semantics.
Finality can be presented as authorization.
Finality can be presented as civic authority.
A historical finality record can outlive its currentness.
A mutable latest registry can be offered instead of exact evidence.
